 ORDER
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 seeking enchancement OF compensation by Rs.2 lakhs.

2. Learned Fourth Additional, MACT, Morena in Case No.53/2010 by award dated 30.09.2010 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act on account of the motor accident dated 25.12.2009 near Nayagaon Dist - Morena by the offending vehicle-Tractor bearing No. MP 07 H 4382 owned by respondent No.1/Pancham Singh driven by respondent No.2-Tarachand insured with respondent No.3 causing death of Ram Niwas aged about 30 years who was stated to be an electrician cum milk seller and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
3.
The learned Tribunal after trial awarded a compensation of Rs.3,92,300/-.

Smt. Kamla vs Pancham Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104842025/
2 4.

It is submitted that on the date of accident the deceased-Ram Niwas along with relative Mahesh was going on motorcycle and respondent No.2 drove the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the deceased, causing severe injury to the deceased which ultimately resulted in death.

5. The accident was reported in Police Station- Bamore and a case was registered under Section 304A of IPC in Crime No.195/09 and the charge-sheet was filed after investigation before the learned JMFC, Morena bearing Case No.2808/09.
6. The respondent No.1 and 2 in their written statement denied the factum of accident by their vehicle.

Insurance Company in their written statement submitted that tractor was being used by respondent No.1 and 2 as a loading vehicle which was not covered under Insurance Policy and therefore, denied their liability.
7. The grounds of the appeal are that less compensation has been awarded therefore, it should be enhanced by Rs.2 Lacs.
8. Learned counsel for respondent No.1, 2 and 3 opposed any enhancement.

9. Respondent No.1 & 2 has filed cross objection by IA No.747/2011 and it is submitted that without any evidence, the learned Tribunal assuming the income of the decease at Rs.2800/- per month awarded a compensation of Rs.3,92,300/- by applying the multiply of 17.
Accident was caused by unknown vehicle.

There was no age proof in fact the age of the deceased should be taken as 50 years,
there was no valid driving license with respondent No.2 therefore, appeal should be dismissed and if any compensation is not paid, let it be paid by Insurance Company.
10(i) The question before this Court whether the amount of compensation can be enhanced.
(ii) Whether liability of paying compensation can be shifted to respondent No.3-Insurance Company by exonerating respondent No.1 and 2 i.e. owner and driver of the vehicle.
11. Perused the record considered the arguments.
12. In Claims Tribunal regarding Issue No.5 whether breach of Insurance Policy is proved.
13. Learned Tribunal has recorded a finding that Insurance Policy breach is proved.

The Insurance Company has produced their witness NA.01 (C.Tirki), the Manager of National Insurance Company Limited who has stated that Exhibit-D/3 is driver's licence particulars valid upto 29/12/2005 only and therefore there was breach of Insurance Policy (Exhibit-D/1) on the date of accident i.e.
25.12.2009.

The R.T.O. Clerk- Shri Dilip Kumar Non-applicant Witness No.2 of Insurance Company and Naval Kishore (Non-Applicant Witness No.3)-Investigator have stated that as per policy D-1,
the driver should have had valid driving license but at the time of accident, there was no valid driving license to drive the vehicle and for that they have called particulars of the driving license (Exhibit-D/3) which proves that on the date of accident dated 25.12.2009 there was no driving Smt.Kamla vs Pancham Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104842025/
3 license in fact, the driving license was only for the period 30.12.2002 to 29.12.2005.
After the accident, a renewal application for driving license was made on 12.07.2010.

14. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 and 2 submitted that when Pancham-owner of Truck had hired had seen the driving license but that would not suffice if had actually seen the license, because if he had seen the licence he would have also seen that it was valid till 29th December, 2005 only especially when there is no reliable evidence as to when he hired the services of the driver i.e.
respondent No.2 (Tarachand).
15.

Learned Tribunal in paragraphs 15 and 16 has considered the rival contentions of both the parties and the citations submitted by him in this regard, and when on the date of accident no application for renewal was pending therefore, it has correctly held that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation as breach of policy (Exhibit-D/1) is proved.

16. Learned counsel for respondents No.1 & 2 (cross-objector) at the time of argument submitted that in view of High Court of Madhya Pradesh judgment in MA No.532/2013 [Smt.Gudiya and others vs. Govind Sharma and others] decided on 03.5.2019 wherein in paragraph 11 pay and recovery can be granted.

entities.text: Smt.Gudiya and others vs. Govind Sharma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, prayer of respondent No.1 and 2 to shift the liability on respondent No.3-Insurance Company is rejected in facts and circumstances but pay and recover can be ordered.

17. Regarding the enhancement of claim, it is seen that learned Tribunal has awarded on lower side,
actually the calculation would be as such:-
(i) Income of deceased on date of accident - Rs.3750 25.12.2009 as per minimum wages applicable in State of Madhya Pradesh (ii) Addition of future prospects in income - Rs.5250/-
@ 40% since deceased was less than 40 years Rs.3750 (Rs.3750 X 40%)
(iii) Annual income of deceased (Rs.5250 X 12)- Rs.63,000/-
(iv) Personal living expense (1/5th of Income)- Rs.12,600/-
(v) Deduction towards personal living expense - Rs.50,400/-
(Rs.63,000 - Rs.12,600)
(vi) Multiplier applied considering age as 30 years - 17 (vii) Income dependency of family - Rs.8,56,800/-
 (Rs.50,400 X 17)
( viii) Loss of estate - Rs.1 Smt.Kamla vs Pancham Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104842025/
4  (ix) Funeral expenses - Rs.1  (x) Loss of consortium -

Total compensation Rs.12,06,800/-
18.

The Tribunal has already awarded compensation of Rs.3,92,300/-, therefore, enhanced amount of compensation to which the appellants/claimants would be entitled comes to Rs.8,14,500/-
(Rs.12,06,800 - Rs.3,92,300/-).
However, initially the appellants had valued the appeal at Rs.4 lacs but as per order of this Court dated 18.10.2014 amended the valuation from Rs.4 lacs to Rs.2 lacs.
The appellants on valuation of Rs.2 lacs paid court fee of Rs.5,000/- as per office note dated 31.10.2014.

Hence, appellants would only be entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2 lacs only in view of decision of this Court in the case of Manoj Kumar and others Vs. HDFC and others [M.A.No.155/2019 decided on 17.4.2023].

Other findings of the impugned award shall remain intact.
